utterances.text: Was either of the expressions you used just now the same expression as "Joint Command"?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, "objedinjeno komandovanje," combined command, is mentioned in P1995. It was said that combined command was embodied in the Joint Command. I think it was an analysis of the Jeskovo action that concerned MUP and the army, and I can perhaps show that exhibit. That would be easier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No. I just want to be clear. Everyone seems to read "Joint Command" as something rather different from "combined command." That's my only reason for asking. But it's the word "Joint Command" that seems to spread terror in the ranks, rather than "combined command." And I just want it to be clear that we weren't discussing the same word again. So please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Well, to clarify things, we can maybe just cast a brief look at this exhibit, to make things even clearer.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: General, when you say "combined command through a joint command of the MUP and the army," this is something that we saw in those analyses that you made. I don't want to open this document, so that we can move forward more efficiently, but can you please explain that?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that I, as the commander of the army, and he, as the commander of the MUP, are in the same location. We're close to each other. He's in command of his units; I'm in command of my units. Together we monitor this activity, and if necessary, if his units need support, he comes to me and asks for it directly from me. And I can directly issue an order to my unit to provide this support to him. In practice, it turned out, in my case, to have been the most economical and the most effective way to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just to clarify things --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Could we have the third page of this document which we see right now on our screens. The last page, please, in B/C/S. I think that the page before the last one in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please look at that. In English, that's the last passage; and in B/C/S, or in Serbian, that's the first sentence on the page that you have in front of you. Could you please read the second sentence, "The commanding over the envisaged forces was combined ...."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The exercise of command over the envisaged forces was combined with the joint command of the forces of the MUP and the VJ." So that's precisely what I've been explaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do, is that sentence you've just read, is it in the English on the page we've got on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: But the translation is -- it is the -- it is on the bottom of the -- bottom of the page, last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And it is the wrong word for "objedinjeno," which we call in Serbian language "objedinjeno".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So are you saying the word in the second-last line on the page should be "combined," rather than "joint" in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: "combined by joint command," to be more precise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, I'm not understanding, then. Mr. Delic, would you read that sentence again, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "The exercise of command over the envisaged forces was combined by a joint command of the MUP and VJ forces," or "through or under."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's just clarify one more thing while we're on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the first page, please, of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, we don't have to read it. You have it in front of you on your screen. It says here in the first sentence that you provided support to the MUP forces pursuant to an order of the Pristina Corps Command, strictly confidential number 455-63, dated the 23rd of March, 1999. Is that one of those documents bearing the heading of the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is one of those orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, sir, my colleague Mr. Lukic asked you about the action in the villages of Bela Crkva and Celina, and you drew them -- drew in the movement of the MUP units on the map, and on that occasion you stated that this was the 23rd PJP Detachment. I found that a bit confusing. And could we just clarify this through these documents. Could we have P2015 on our screens, please. Could we please see paragraph 4 and paragraph 5.1 on our screens. In paragraph 5.1, is there any specific MUP unit referred to in the tasks of supporting your unit, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I can see, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have a look at 1981, P1981, rather. General, did you write this order on the basis of the previous document that we saw on our screens?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we please have a look at paragraph 4. General, in paragraph 4 we see that what is planned here is an action with the 37th Detachment of the PJP; however, later you indicated that this was the 23rd Detachment of the PJP and you highlighted that it was the 23rd, not the 37th Detachment, as referred to here in this order.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In this activity, it was both the 37th and the 23rd that were involved. The 37th participated with the main forces from the axis of Suva Reka, and only with one company from Combat Group 6 from Orahovac, from my units. The 5th and the 6th Company of the PJP were engaged in other tasks. I did not know about that at that moment of coordination. So the MUP sent this 23rd Detachment that was active along the axis that I drew, indicated yesterday with part of the forces, and another part of the forces were in the area between Mala Krusa and the village of Pirane.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would like to know the following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you mean to refer to the 5th and the 4th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Although they are indicated here in my order, this is what had been agreed upon at the coordination meeting. Afterwards, however, the chief of the secretariat called me and told me that these units would not take part; however, that they would regulate this and that the 23rd Detachment of the PJP from Djakovica would carry out this combat action instead of them, and that is who appeared on that axis on the following day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very briefly, General. We saw these documents with the heading where it says "Joint Command." Until when were you receiving these documents?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that I got only a few documents, but this was in April. The last document that I got has to do with Jezerce.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you know why later on you did not receive such documents?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, around the 20th of April an order on re-subordination came, and that is when this process ensued. One order, another order, attempts to carry out re-subordination, which did not take place. At any rate, these orders were no longer there, those that bore the heading "Joint Command."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Did re-subordination take place?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Re-subordination did not take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, Mr. Hannis asked you in detail about a Prosecution exhibit, P2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please have it displayed on our screens. It is an analysis of the activity of crushing STS in the Malisevo-Pagarusa area. So could I please have page 2 in the B/C/S version -- or rather, in Serbian, and page 3 in English. The one-but-last paragraph in English. In Serbian it is the fifth paragraph, the fifth from the top, that starts with the following words: "During the course of the third day ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: So if you look at the last part of this paragraph, you indicate that evacuation was carried out and that about 30.000 refugees were taken care of. You did say that you were not in the village of Belanica. I would be interested in the following: Did you perhaps have information about inhumane treatment of civilians?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not have such information. I've already said yesterday that in front of me, in front of my units, part of the population had left in that direction and another part came forward to my unit on this asphalt road between Malisevo and Orahovac. But I do not have such information, especially for Belanica, because I was not there personally and none of my officers went there either, because this was outside the area of activity of my unit. This is on the axis of my neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Those were all my questions. Once again, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Trial Chamber and legal officer confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry about that delay, Mr. Delic. I just wanted to be sure that there weren't any other areas that we wish to explore with you. That completes your evidence. Thank you for coming again to the Tribunal to give it. You are now free to leave the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Our next witness is General Momir Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration to speak the truth by reading aloud the document which will now be shown to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You will now be examined by Mr. Bakrac, who appears for Mr. Lazarevic. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We've already introduced you, but could you please do so for the record. Could you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Momir -- Momir Stojanovic, father's name Bogovid. I am a retired general.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us where and when you were born?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 12th of October, 1958 in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, which duties did you perform in your military career?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In my professional career, I performed all the duties in the military intelligence service -- in the military security service from the operations officer to the head of the military security agency of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro. I was also -- I held all the command posts up to the level of the corps commander. Chief of Staff of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And when did you retire?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to tell us, how long did you serve in Kosovo and Metohija and what post did you hold there?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In Kosovo and Metohija I served between 1993 and 1999. First I was the deputy chief of the security department in the Pristina Corps Command, and later on I became the chief of the security department in the Pristina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, our time is limited, so I will be asking you questions only about the relevant period. So could you please tell us, in 1998 and 1999 which post did you hold in that period?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 and 1999 I was the chief of the security department in the Pristina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell us, what is the role of the military security service organs in the chain of command of the army?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The organs of the military security service are professional organs of the command. They're immediately subordinate to the unit commander, but along the professional line they are subordinated to the chief of the security organ in the command that is immediately superior. So during 1998 and 1999, in professional terms the chief of the security section of the 3rd Army was in charge and in command of the security department in the Pristina Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let me just warn you about something. I'm -- if I make a pause, I make a pause in order to wait for the interpretation to be finished, so I'm not waiting for you to complete your answer. What you just told us, does that mean that in professional terms, or in technical terms, you were in charge of all the security organs in the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In addition to the security organs in the Pristina Corps, in 1998 and 1999 were there any other military security service organs in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to the military security service organs in the Pristina Corps, in 1998 and 1999 in Kosovo and Metohija there were also the organs of the military security service of the command of the military district in Pristina. And in professional or technical terms, they were subordinate to the intelligence section of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's Correction: Security section of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were also the organs of the 14th Counter-intelligence Group both in terms of command and technical terms, it was under the security administration of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell us, how were the military security service organs manned in the commands and in the units of the Pristina Corps in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 the military security service organs were present in all the organisational units of the Pristina Corps, down to the level of the Independent Battalion. Because of the complex security situation on the state border with the Republic of Albania and the overall security situation in the territory, the security administration of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro in June 1998 reinforced the organs of the Pristina Corps by sending some personnel, experienced operations officers, and from that time on the military security service organs were present in all the organisational units of the Pristina Corps, down to the level of combat group and border post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell us, what are the basic tasks of the military security service organs when it came to terrorism and terrorist activities in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The task of the military security service organs when it came to terrorism was to detect, document, and stop anti-terrorist, subversive, and any other illegal activities in commands, units, and installations of the Pristina Corps or aimed against them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, what powers did the organs of the military security service have?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In accordance with Article 30 of the Law on the Army of Yugoslavia, the organs of the military security service have the right, the power, and the duty that corresponds to those of the organs of the interior. Again, in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure and the Law on Military Courts, the organs of the military security service participate in the actions that precede the institution of criminal proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we spoke about powers. Those powers that organs of the military security service have, against whom could they use them?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: They could use them against all the personnel of the Army of Yugoslavia and all those persons involved in hostile activities targeting the commands, units, and installations of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell us, what are the powers of the military security service organs vis-a-vis the military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The organs of the military security service, in technical and professional terms, are in charge of the military police organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do the military security service organs have the right to issue orders to the military police?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. Only the commander of the unit that has military police units within its formation have the right to do so. The military security service organs propose to the commander of such a unit how the military police units are to be -- should be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What are the obligations of the security organs in the units of the Pristina Corps vis-a-vis the commanders of those units?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The military security service organs are professional organs of the appropriate commands, units, and installations of the Army of Yugoslavia, and they are subordinate to the commanders of those units. But in professional terms, in technical terms, as I've already indicated, they are subordinate to the chief of the security organ in the immediate command that is immediately superior to the one where they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What measures may a military security organ propose in relation to these persons?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The organs of the military security service have to report to their -- to their unit commander about any hostile or other illegal activities that have already been carried out or is expected to be carried out either in units and also against the units, facilities, or personnel of those units. On the basis of the assessments and analyses, they propose to the unit commanders measures to be taken so that the hostile activities can be documented and sanctioned and also measures that are to be taken to prevent the expected hostile activities or to reduce the consequences thereof.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "measures that are to be taken," what measures are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I am referring specifically to specific measures to be taken in a specific unit. They can be organisational in nature. They may pertain to personnel. They can be disciplinary measures or even a criminal prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, did you -- and if yes -- as the chief of the security department report about the activities of the security organ? And if so, to whom did you report?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As the chief of the security department in the Pristina Corps Command, I reported every day on the results of the work of our organs to the corps commander. Also, every day I would send a telegram up the technical chain of command to the security section in the 3rd Army command and to the security administration of the General Staff of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro. But when NATO aggression against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia started, I reported only to the security section of the 3rd Army about the results of my work. In the later period, those telegrams of mine were accompanied by proper documents, in the proper format as envisaged by the rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were the reports to the 3rd Army command security section and the security administration of the General Staff identical?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, could you please tell us briefly how these telegrams were structured.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The telegrams that the Pristina Corps Command security department sent during 1998 and 1999 to those addressees contained three parts: The first part pertained to the security situation at the state border; the second part pertained to the security situation in the territory; and the third part pertained to the security situation in the units and commands of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You mentioned the situation in the territory as part -- being part of those telegrams. What I want to know is whether the security organs were in fact in charge of the security situation in the territory.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. They were in charge -- or rather, the situation in the territory was something that other organs dealt with; primarily the organs of the Ministry of the Interior and the organs of the State Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we move on to the next question, I'm wondering if I heard wrongly or if there's an error in the transcript. I think at page 60, Line 21 it is recorded here: "When the NATO aggression against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia started, I reported only to the security section of the 3rd Army about the results of my work." I thought you said you reported only to the security section of the General Staff. But maybe I'm in error. Would we -- could we clarify now, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, can you clarify that point. You said that the situation was different once the NATO aggression started. You reported only with -- by telegram to only one organ. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me clarify. In 1998 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, just -- just please answer the question. The position changed when the aggression started in March 1999, and you said in your earlier answer that at that stage you reported only to the security section of ... Now, was it the 3rd Army or the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The security section of the 3rd Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your answer was accurately recorded, you will be relieved to know. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, let us be clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What is the reason you meant to clarify? What is the reason this changed with the beginning of the aggression?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Normally, along professional lines, the security section of the Pristina Corps should report about the results of its work to the immediately superior organ; that's the security section of the 3rd Army. However, on orders of the chief of the security administration of the General Staff of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro, in the course of 1998 and all the way until the NATO aggression started, I reported the same contents with the same telegram to the security section of the 3rd Army and the security administration of the General Staff. After the NATO aggression started, on orders of the chief of the security administration of the General Staff, I was only duty-bound to report to the security section of the 3rd Army command.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, you explained who was responsible for the state of security in the territory, and that's where my learned friend Mr. Stamp intervened. I would like to know why in your reports to the superiors you reported on the security situation in the territory. We saw you said it was one of the elements in your reports.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The security situation in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija was part of my reports because in the course of 1998 but also in 1999, in terms of intensity and forms of its manifestation, Kosovo and Metohija witnessed the most brutal form of terrorism, which at all times endangered commands, units, installations, and members of the army of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and they were precisely those who are meant to be protected by the security organs of the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in the course of this trial we have reviewed quite a lot of your telegrams from 1998. I would like to move to that subject briefly and to show you a number of documents. There are many of them, but we will look only at a few of them. It seems that they come from you personally. I would like to know what kind of information the military security service had about the arming of Albanian terrorists in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: As for the arming of Albanian terrorists in Kosovo and Metohija, the military security service of the Pristina Corps had information that after the dissolution of state institutions in the Republic of Albania, after the break-up of pyramid financing and savings schemes, there occurred a dissolution of all institutions, including the army and the police. Under those circumstances, an enormous arsenal from the depots of the Albanian army came into the possession of numerous gangs, primarily in the north of Albania, and then these weapons, through illegal channels in end 1997 and especially in the first half of 1998, were intensively smuggled into Kosovo and Metohija. The general standards in the area of Albania were such that poverty was rampant and there was a lot of money in the area of Kosovo and Metohija, so these weapons were purchased and sometimes even given as a present to members of terrorist units in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: At that time, in 1996, 1997, 1998, were there any border posts on the Albanian side, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. In end 1996 and throughout 1997 and into 1997 -- 1998, the gangs in the north of Albania looted some of the border posts facing our country, burnt them, and from that time on not a single border post on the border of Albania with the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was manned, and regular border service did not function.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, when, according to your information, did there occur a more massive incursion of terrorists from the territory of Albania and their major grouping in the area of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Individual incursions of smaller groups of Albanian terrorists from the territory of Albania to the territory of Kosovo and Metohija began back in March 1998, and it became massive, in groups of up to 100 terrorists, or hundreds of terrorists, and their spillover across the state border began later in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at 5D1304. That is apparently a report of the security section of the 3rd Army, dated 18 April 1998. It seems to have been compiled by Colonel Petar Kuzmanovic. Could you please look at this document and comment on it briefly and tell us whether it was compiled based on your operative information, your intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this was written based on the intelligence in the position of the security organs of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, one of the reasons why we are opening this document is a mistake we have in the translation of the date. In English we see "1996," and in the original it's "1998".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We can note that and move on, unless there's something else you want to deal with in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. General, could you give us a brief comment on these -- on this document from April 1998. Is this the intelligence you had at your disposal?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This document pertains to the organisation of illegal smuggling of arms and military equipment from the territory of Albania to Kosovo and Metohija. Such intelligence reports came in every day. This particular document pertains to the intervention and conduct of Albanian citizens on both sides of the border involving illegal smuggling of weapons, naming persons who are involved, but it also covers information that points to the presence of foreign nationals who are illegally coming in and are present within terrorist groups in Kosovo and Metohija, primarily from Islamic countries. That is the kind of intelligence we had throughout 1998 and 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, this problem of massive illegal incursions of terrorists and arms smuggling, how did you deal with it from the viewpoint of your prescribed duties?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly for the security organs of the Pristina Corps and the overall organs of command of the Pristina Corps this was a very grave security problem, since we knew that through illegal channels persons from Kosovo and Metohija were sent regularly for training to North Albania in order to be returned after training and arming into Kosovo and Metohija. Our security organs facing this problem detached one group of experienced operatives and a group of officers combatting crime from the military police to a forward command post, and their job was to interrogate and process the terrorists who were arrested and to deal with problems on the state border, the forward command post of Djakovica, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Was there any criminological and forensic investigation into each border incident?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Each incident on our state border with Albania was processed fully, in terms of on-site investigation and compiling the necessary criminological and forensic documentation. That practice continued throughout, including after the arrival of the KVM.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you mentioned the OSCE mission, did you report to them about each border incident? Did they come to inspect the location?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the liaison officers in the subordinate units of the command of the Pristina Corps, as well as the liaison team with the mission of the OSCE attached to the command of the Pristina Corps, regularly informed the mission of the OSCE about all border incidents, and almost in every case representatives of the OSCE mission visited the location. In contacts with the competent investigative organs and organs of the command, they regularly emphasised appropriate work of our investigative organs of the state border with Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: How were the arrested terrorists treated in these border incidents?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The terrorists whom the security organs on the state border arrested when they attempted to illegally cross the state border one way or another, in one direction or another, were turned over through local competent commissions to the security authorities, but prior to that interviews were conducted with them, and later on, together with all their belongings, their statements and other documents found on them, they were turned over to the competent authorities of the Ministry of the Interior, with a proviso that those terrorists who opened fire while attempting to illegally cross the state border at our border authorities, wounding or killing a member of the Army of Yugoslavia, were turned over to the military prosecutors of the competent military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in addition to these illegal transfers of terrorists and weapons from the territory of Albania, were there any other activities of terrorists in Kosovo and Metohija? And if so, what did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In addition to the smuggling of weapons, military equipment, and illegal border crossings of terrorists from Albania into Kosovo and Metohija, the information we had in the security organ of the Pristina Corps pointed to intensive activity of terrorist groups in the area of Kosovo and Metohija itself. It manifested itself primarily in the evacuation of certain populated areas with a majority Albanian population, so that these settlements can be fortified and prepared for defence. After that, the terrorists would impose a curfew in such places, that is, introduced restrictions on the movement of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be a good idea while you are saying this to look at 3D994. That seems to be one of your reports. I would appreciate your comments. I'll repeat. 3D994. Do you recognise this report?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If we could just make the lettering larger. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is this your report to the security administration of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia to the security section of the 3rd Army command and to the security organ of the 14th Counter-Intelligence Group?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of the 10th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: To move on more quickly, could you concentrate on paragraph 5 from the top.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The fifth paragraph in the document before us presents our processing of intelligence, indicating the terrorist units are evacuating women, children, and elderly men from villages in the territory of Djakovica municipality, leaving behind armed terrorists who are preparing for armed combat. I want to emphasise that this intelligence also indicates some of the reasons for the migration of population in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Could you now look at the eighth and the ninth paragraph and tell us something about that.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: "Information indicates or intelligence indicates that on the 15th of June, it is expected that a state of war will be proclaimed and the KLA will engage large-scale armed action." I want to emphasise that this refers -- this telegram refers to the 16th of June, 1998, when brutal terrorist actions of the so-called Liberation Army of Kosovo, almost 40 per cent of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija were placed under KLA control, and it is in this light that we should view their intentions in the wake of the proclamation of the state of war. They were probably aware of their strength and the control they achieved.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said actions in anticipation of the state of war proclamation. Tell us, who was supposed to proclaim the state of war?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The leadership of the Kosovo Liberation Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What kind of secret police was established in Djakovica, as we see in the next paragraph?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On a parallel track with the evacuation of certain settlements in the area of Djakovica municipality, where in addition to the Drenica region, intensive terrorism began, smaller units of a secret military police of the KLA were formed, and they would later grow into the military police of the KLA, headed by Fatmir Limaj, known under the pseudonym Celiku. Those armed group, as we see from this telegram, after the forced mobilisation of Albanians was proclaimed, served to intimidate the population and more specifically, the persons who refused to join the armed units of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let us now look at another telegram, 3D998. Could you just comment. This is another one of your telegrams. The last two paragraphs. The penultimate paragraph. In the area of Sopot village.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: "As a result of the exchange of information with the SUP of Prizren, we received information that armed terrorists appeared in the area of Sopot village, municipality of Djakovica, and they exerted pressure on local residents to leave the village." That's what I was talking about before. It says also that "Electronic surveillance produced information indicating that on the border between Yugoslavia and Albania from the Albanian side there is organised admission of citizens of Siptar nationality from Kosovo and Metohija who are then directed towards Bajram Curi, where an admission centre is located. There are also training centres for terrorists." What is important here, that the terrorists in the north of Albania performed selection among the incoming citizens from Kosovo and Metohija separating men who can be trained and place other citizens in different locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, is the date of that the 18th of June, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, 16th of June, 1998. If we are talking about 3D998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, it's -- the stamp has the 18th, but that may be a date of receipt. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, or maybe the -- I can ask the witness to tell you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can, if I may, Your Honour. This stamp bears the date of the 18th. That is the date when it was received at the security administration of the General Staff of the army and when it was registered there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we can move on. The telegram of this witness, 3D997 pertains to the same subject. There's no need to open it again. I would like to now look at one document, 5D1305, that we haven't seen before in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's your telegram dated 18 July 1998. Just give us a brief comment before we adjourn for the break.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... was a translation of this document provided to us? Well, there's one here. I just saw that. There's one.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was informed that everything for this witness and the next two of my witnesses has been translated. We followed your suggestions. We showered the CLSS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's there. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: May I just indicate I rose because we had not had translation up until yesterday. Perhaps this came into the system early. But I can work with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please look at this and give us a comment on the first, second, and third paragraphs of this telegram. It looks like it is one of yours. Is it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's my telegram dated 18 July 1998. The first paragraph deals with the attack of the terrorists on the town of Orahovac itself. Let me emphasise again, it's end June, beginning of July, when the terrorist leaders believed that they were so strong that they could attack Orahovac itself. They attacked the health centre, kidnapped several dozen, around 30 Serbs, seized medical supplies from the health centre, and I believe nothing more was ever heard of these people, as far as I know. The next paragraph also describes a border incident on the Kosare border post, where the location was searched and arrested persons were searched and documentation was found showing that in the ranks of the KLA they -- there were also foreign nationals from Saudi Arabia, from Yemen, and six nationals of Saudi Arabia who somehow procured for themselves passports of the Republic of Macedonia. This shows that there were mercenaries fighting for the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, it seems that in this paragraph -- could you just explain that. Is it -- is my reading correct? It seems that at one point a group of 700 terrorists attempted to cross the border illegally and come into Kosovo and Metohija, resulting in an armed skirmish.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, this figure is correct. Later on through the following telegrams and after interviews of some terrorists who were arrested, we came to this figure of that group that attempted to come in on that day. This shows the dramatic state of security on the state border with Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Just one brief question before we have to adjourn for the break. We can move to page 2. But it seems from your report that the terrorists took control of the town of Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In this action, they managed to reach the centre of Orahovac, where in one building around 250 policemen were surrounded and they could not get out unless there was an intervention of other security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe this is a good time for the break, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We do have to break at this stage, Mr. Stojanovic. That will be for an hour. Could you leave the courtroom, please, along with the usher and we will see you again at 1.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us proceed where we broke off. I would be interested in the following: All of these reports came from your security organ from the 3rd Army. What about the security organs of other strategic groups -- or rather, armies of the Army of Yugoslavia had any knowledge about the activity of Albanian terrorists in the territory of their own areas of responsibility respectively? And while you are talking, I would like to call up 3D1000.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. Before all knowledge concerning activities, plans, and intentions of the Albanian terrorists in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, it was first and foremost that the security organs of the 2nd Army district in Podgorica that had this information and knowledge, because the area of responsibility of that army bordered with the state border towards Albania. Therefore, there was a problem of securing that part of the state border, vis-a-vis the Republic of Albania was a problem, and it was within the remit of the Podgorica Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: When you say "the Podgorica Corps," what republic is that?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The Republic of Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Please, now we have in front of us 3D1000. Could you have a look and could you give us your comments on the second and third paragraphs. And could you tell us whether you received this kind of information from the command of the 2nd Army -- or rather, their security organ.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I did receive this information. And in the second paragraph of the document that is in front of us, there is a reference to two arrested citizens of the Republic of Albania, and you can see that they are 18 and even 14 years old. In this case, they were reconnoitering of the state border belt in order to prepare the terrain for the entry of a larger group of terrorists, and that, as I said, is the area of responsibility of the Podgorica Corps. This shows that Albanian terrorists even used 14-year-old children to attain their own objectives and such risky efforts like crossing the state border illegally. Also, in the third paragraph of the document that is in front of us, there is a reference to what I testified about a few moments ago, and that is the taking in of Albanian refugees in the territory of the Republic of Albania. Also, a selection of these refugees, and the sending of military-age citizens, able-bodied, to centres that had already been established in the north of Albania, where terrorists from Kosovo and Metohija had already been trained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we see the end of this document, please. How was this information relayed to you, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This information was cc'd to me from the security department of the 3rd Army, and it probably came from the security administration of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, do you know that at that time, in 1998, the villagers from Albanian villages -- certain Albanian villages in Kosovo and Metohija turned to the Army of Yugoslavia for protection against the growing number of terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, there are many such examples, especially in the spring of 1998, when there was a great deal of activity on the part of Albanian terrorists in many localities in Kosovo and Metohija. The representatives of the Army of Yugoslavia, in this case specifically the units of the Pristina Corps, were addressed by the local population of some villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can you give us some examples?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. The citizens of the villages of Brovina, Batusa, Korenica turned to the Army of Yugoslavia. All of these villages are in the territory of the municipality of Djakovica and all of them are in the border belt in the area facing Albania. But such requests also came from villagers in the Dragas municipality. I can say, with your permission -- I can, rather, give another example, say the villagers from Batusa, which is in the border belt facing Albania, and that is where the only road leading to our border post of Karaula facing the border of Albania, that's the only road. So the local villagers asked the army to protect them from activities -- or rather, from the terror of the KLA. I personally interviewed eminent and influential members of that village community, and then, together with the commander of the Pristina Corps, General Pavkovic, and the Chief of Staff of the Pristina Corps, General Lazarevic, I attended a meeting between the villagers and the representatives of the army in which an agreement was reached to the effect that the army would ensure the security of the villagers of those villages and, in turn, the villagers asked the army to protect them from mistreatment at the hands of Albanian terrorists from the village of Junik, which was a neighbouring village and which was near the village of Batusa. During the night they would break into the village and pressure the villagers to receive weapons, and they would search their premises and ask them for money to buy weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: On that occasion, was some aid given to this village? And could you tell us what happened after that contact with you and those activities.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Agreement was reached. These are very honourable, loyal people, a very honourable, loyal community, Albanian community. Then the corps commander ordered -- well, this was on other occasions too, but now that I'm talking about this village, I remember that his order was to help this village in terms of basic food supplies and medical assistance, and that was certainly done. However, a few days after this agreement was reached, one of the representatives of the mentioned village, and the most influential person from that village, Zenal Batusa, who took part in the negotiations with the representatives of the military, when he set out for the town Djakovica, he was kidnapped in a deceitful way by a terrorist from the terrorist stronghold of Junik, and we did not know what his fate was after that. On the following day, the villagers of that village, out of fear, started moving out in an organised way to the town of Djakovica itself. The representatives of the military, including myself, asked them and gave them guarantees yet again that they would provide for their security. However, they feared further reactions of the terrorists from the village of Junik and then they moved out in a collective manner to the very centre of the town of Djakovica. This is yet another example of the reasons for the relocation of the Albanian population in Kosovo and Metohija during 1998.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, are there documents about this?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. But there is a videoclip which, by mistake, was omitted from our list. With your leave -- I'm not going to finish today for sure, but with your permission, could we deal with that video clip tomorrow morning? There are other documents, and this video clip has to do with that particular meeting that we discussed, and there are other issues that I wish to raise with this witness in this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm sorry, if we're going to deal with the video clip, is that what I see here? And since it's raised now, can we be notified as to what it's about and given a copy or something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sure that's going to happen, Mr. Stamp, and the issue will not arise until tomorrow, so let's proceed at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this afternoon we are going to send this to Mr. Stamp so that he can be ready. I'm just asking you for permission, because it's not on our list. To err is human, as they say. It just so happened that this video clip is not included on our list. So with your permission, yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the -- the permission will depend upon the impact that the late notification might have on the Prosecution, so we'll hear about that tomorrow. The main thing for you is to disclose it, its identity, as quickly as possible so that they can check their position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. While we are waiting for the fate of this video clip, let us look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're not waiting on its fate. You can deal with that behind the scenes. Just let's proceed, and tomorrow morning Mr. Stamp will tell us whether he objects to you using it or not. If -- if it takes you until then to reach it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I meant. I was misunderstood. But let's not waste any time. 3D996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CHOWHAN
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt. I think you didn't use the proverb correctly, fully. And that would have impressed Mr. Stamp. "To forgive is divine" was the other part of it, and that would convince him more.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I accept that, Your Honour. I take all the blame. Yes. 3D996.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, while we are waiting for this exhibit to appear in e-court, I think that it is a telegram of yours, in actual fact, very often in this courtroom we heard of the village of Korenica. Could you please take a look at this document now, and I would like you to pay particular attention to the third paragraph. Is this your telegram?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Go ahead. Give us your comments.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You asked me about the third paragraph. It says in it that: "On the basis of intelligence received, the people of Korenica village in the municipality of Djakovica are prepared to ask the Army of Yugoslavia for protection. During the course of the day, the security organs of the Pristina Corps established contact with influential persons from the mentioned village. They were informed of our request that they not receive weapons and they were given security guarantees by our units. The villagers asked for time for consultation, so the next contact or a meeting was scheduled for the 16th of June this year."

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Tell us, what happened after that? This is quite clear, what is written here and what you read out us to. What happened then?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In this specific case, like in many other cases, when the leaders of terrorist groups of the KLA in Kosovo and Metohija would receive information about any kind of talks between the inhabitants of local Albanian villages and when they were saying that they were not prepared to take weapons, they would exercise influence over these villagers and even threaten them openly to give up on that altogether. In this specific case, during the course of the night, after our talks, from the terrorist stronghold of the village of Nec in the municipality of Djakovica, which functioned within the 137th Brigade of the Kosovo Liberation Army, headquartered in the village of Ramoc, not far away from that village the representatives of that terrorist staff came and threatened the inhabitants of the mentioned village, telling them to stop all further communication with the representatives of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, now I'm going to put a question to you. We heard testimony from a protected witness here, a K witness. Was pressure brought to bear against Muslim members of the army, and are you aware of any such cases?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you -- before you go on to explain that, I didn't realize we were finished with this document. What was the source of your information about the threatening of the inhabitants of the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, our operative positions that were throughout the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, and in this specific region, reported to us on this. Later on a local inhabitant of that village, an elderly man, admitted that to me personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In what context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He admitted that, saying that two or three young men from that village had already been in this staff in the village of Nec and had received arms, weapons, and that they had received a message through those young men not to continue with their negotiations with the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But how did you meet this -- this villager?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I met with this villager legally, the inhabitant of the village of Korenica, because this village is -- it's the first village next to the municipality of Djakovica, close to the bridge at Erenik and the forward command post of the corps, and this village was not affected by any terrorist activities. And later on I ordered my subordinates, security organs to verify this information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there must be some misunderstanding between us. How was it you came to be speaking to this person? Did he come to you? Did you go to him? Did you just happen to come across him in the street? What -- how did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes. Now I understand you, Your Honour. I went to his house in the village of Korenica. It was an eminent villager, and I talked to him in his yard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, at the beginning we provided this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But let me ask you: General, your place of birth, how far is it from the village of Korenica?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I was born in Djakovica, and that's -- that's the first village. If you move from Djakovica in the direction of the state border with Albania, that's the first village. That's, for all intents and purposes, a village that would be part of the town of Djakovica were it not for the River Erenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you completed your elementary and secondary education there.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I completed my elementary and secondary education there, and then I went to attend the military academy from there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that mean you speak Albanian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in 1998 and 1999 I was able to understand Albanian quite well, and I was able to use it. But in the intervening years I have not used it, and my knowledge of Albanian has deteriorated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, we touched upon the topic -- the question was whether there was any pressure on the soldiers of Muslim ethnicity, whether you have any such information. And let us ask for 5D1303. Your telegram is important to us because of the testimony of a protected witness. Could you please comment on the last paragraph on the first page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Units of the Pristina Corps in 1998 and 1999 and indeed in the year -- in the earlier years, were staffed from other garrisons and other training centres, so that in 1998 it received a regular recruitment contingent that -- soldiers that had come from other training centres. This last paragraph pertains to the results of electronic reconnaissance measures where conversations with five soldiers of Muslim ethnicity were intercepted, and a few days before that, as soon as they were transferred from the Valjevo garrison to the 549th Brigade, they deserted. And then measures of electronic reconnaissance were used to record the conversations of these five soldiers. After their desertion, they were in the terrorist staff in the village municipality of Drenovac in the municipality of Orahovac. The parents of those soldiers advised them in order to obtain asylum that they should talk to the authorities there. By that, they meant the authorities in Albania; that they should tell the authorities that the military forced them to kill civilians and children, small children, which was definitely part of the overwhelming propaganda effort.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let us now wrap up with this period and all those terrorist activities. Could we please look at 5D1307. It is your telegram dated the 24th of July, 1998, and it appears to be somewhat longer than the others. Could you please tell us very briefly -- could you please look at the first page and then tell us briefly, what is this telegram about? And then just comment on it very briefly.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This telegram that was written in late July 1998 is an overview of the overall security situation in Kosovo and Metohija. And let me just give you some of the information contained therein. This overview specifies that in March -- in the period between March and June the members of the so-called Kosovo Liberation Army grew in number to 25.000 of armed terrorists. The telegram also specifies the location of the greatest terrorist strongholds, places where there's the biggest concentration of terrorist forces. And it is also stated that they hold approximately 50 per cent of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. And I would like to say that this is the period in which the terrorist units managed to cut off virtually every road leading from Kosovo to Metohija. The only road that could still be used to supply the MUP and military units in the garrisons in Kosovo and Metohija with food and other necessities was the one leading from Strpce and Prizren to the territory of Metohija. In addition to that, in this telegram that I drafted I presented an assessment of the plans, intentions, and activities of the terrorists in the forthcoming period.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us look briefly at page 2, the last-but-one paragraph in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is the fourth paragraph from the bottom in English. It begins with the words, "We have reliable information ..." And it appears that in this telegram the situation regarding Djakovica is also presented.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So could you please just comment briefly whether this is what you talk about in this report too.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This paragraph pertains to the information that was available to us, and that was confirmed several times, that there are about 63 armed terrorists in the village of Ramoc. This number of 63 grew to about 100 terrorists. That was in the end the, 137th KLA Brigade, commanded by Mr. Naim Maloku. They held this entire area under their control -- or rather, this is the area of the villages in Djakovica -- in the hinterland of Djakovica, right next to the Albanian border. This is the belt that is called Caragoj or Reka e Keqe or Llug i Crnagorat. So these are all names for one and the same area that contains the villages of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to list the names a bit more slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, could you go through the names of villages again, please. And when you're dealing with that sort of detail, try to speak a little more slowly to assist the interpreters. But if you could give us the villages where you say "this is the belt that is called," and then you named a number of places. And then you went on to talk about it -- the area containing the villages of, and then there was a list of villages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is a valley behind Cabrat, this is the high ground. It's between Djakovica and the border belt with Albania, and it includes the following villages: Meja, Racaj, Pacaj, Dolosaj, Ramoc, Nivokaz, and further on it goes to the village of Junik. That is the largest village in Metohija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And just for the record, General, what is the name of this valley? You said that it has three names.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, surely I will say. The Albanians call this valley Caragoj and they also called it Reka e Keqe, that would mean bad river, Losa Reka in Serbian, because after the war it was mostly inhabited by Montenegrins and it was also called Llug i Crnagorat, the Montenegrin valley, if you want a translation of that name. General, on page 2 you seem to be talking about the village of Korenica again, and you have information that the people there received weapons.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Just -- I just need some more time to look for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It's the same paragraph. It's at the end of it.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: "The village of Junik is making efforts to arm the village of Korenica and Babaj Boks, although the villagers are trying not to do so, although some of the younger villagers have taken up arms and they're in the village." Is that so?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, let us now leave this period behind. Tell us, please, you made an overview of the situation and what happened then? What was the response to this security situation in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The overall situation in mid-July 1998 was extremely complex and difficult. This assessment of mine, which I believe was made at the request of the security administration of the General Staff of the Army of Serbia and Montenegro, was meant to give an overview of the situation, and soon after that -- I don't know whether this report of mine or whether the information from other sources and security organs present in Kosovo and Metohija played a role in that, but as a result, a comprehensive plan was made to fight terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Until when did the counter-terrorist activity last, the efforts to suppress terrorist hot spots in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The counter-terrorist activities against the terrorists in Kosovo and Metohija, as far as I know, lasted between late July 1998 and the end of September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: After the agreement that established the OSCE mission, the Milosevic-Holbrooke agreement and the establishment of the OSCE mission in Kosovo, did the terrorist activities continue?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, definitely not. As far as I know, on the 13th of October, 1998 the Milosevic-Holbrooke agreement was signed, and after that there was an agreement between the foreign minister of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and the representatives of the OSCE mission. This was an agreement on the deployment of the Kosovo Verification Mission in Kosovo and Metohija. After that, there was an agreement signed between the NATO commander and the chief of the General Staff on the air verification mission. So by -- once these agreements were signed, all the activities on fighting the terrorist hot spots in Kosovo and Metohija stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes, General, but did terrorist activities, activities of the KLA cease once this mission was in place?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I personally believe as I sit here from this vantage point that a mistake was made if the objective was to normalise the situation and to create the best possible security conditions for the life of the population in Kosovo and Metohija. After the OSCE mission was established and after its mandate in Kosovo and Metohija, the terrorist staffs in Kosovo and Metohija did not stop carrying out their terrorist pinpoint actions. They did not stop sending their members to the Republic of Albania illegally to be trained and armed, but the worst thing from the point of view of the security in Kosovo and Metohija is that, as you know, after the signing of this agreement, part of the units that were part of other strategic units of the army that had been re-subordinated to the Pristina Corps left the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. Some of the MUP units, as far as I know, went back to their original locations, leaving behind only some check-points. And what I know for sure is that some combat groups were withdrawn to the barracks. Only a small number of combat groups remained in the border area facing the Republic of Albania, and I think two or three combat groups that were deployed on the roads leading from Kosovo to Metohija on the most critical points. The terrorist staffs exploited this situation to re-take some locations and to put a more compact territory under their control.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you acquaint with the OSCE mission with such activities of the terrorists? Did you inform them of the incidents and violations of the agreement?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I know that at the level of the corps command there was a team for cooperating with the OSCE mission in the province, and it was headed by Colonel Kotur, and one of my duties was to inform the chief of the team, the liaison team, Colonel Kotur, as well as all the other bodies, about the plans and activities of Albanian terrorists for the execution of various actions, terrorist actions, and I believe that he informed the OSCE mission accordingly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 5D1308. And, again, it looks like it's your telegram. But interestingly, it's the 15th of December, 1998, when the OSCE mission has been there for a while. Could you please comment on paras 6 and 4 of this telegram. First of all look at page 1. In item 1, it seems that you invited the OSCE mission to inspect a site of a violation of the state border. And then we will move on to paras 4 and 6.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The first page pertains to the intelligence that we had about the existence of centres, and it says: "Training continues in North Albania, as well as arming." This first page deals in greater detail with the contents of that training in North Albania and the various locations, the duration of the training, and the organisation, the contents of that training.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Look at page 2, please. Forget what I said about paras 4 and 6. It was for another document. Look at paragraphs 3 and 4. It seems that a large group of terrorists tried to break through the state border.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't have the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: It begins with: "On 13 December ..."

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't see the passage on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: The document should be 3D1029 -- no, no, it's the wrong document. 3D1029. I misspoke earlier. 3D1029. Page 2, please. The second page in B/C/S too. "On 13 December," that's the beginning of the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: "On 13 December 1998, around 8.00, a group of about 150 terrorists, led by Gjem Gashi" - he is well known - "departed and arrived at the entrance to the village of Ljubizda Has in early morning hours of 14th of December, 1998 where they were detected by organs protecting the state border." And then it goes on to explain that they were waiting trucks to be transferred to local KLA staffs in the territory. That is consistent with our intelligence that compact groups were formed, sent to Albania. Once armed and trained, they were sent back and placed by terrorists into the various areas of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now look at 5D1308, para 4 and para 6. Comment briefly and then we'll move on. It looks like another one of your telegrams to the security organs of the corps command, dated 16 December 1998.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are the results of interviews with some terrorists who were captured while trying to illegally cross the state border. They confirm how large the group was and they confirm what I said earlier, who was leading which group, that they were divided into various groups, Urosevac, Glodjani, et cetera, groups, which confirms that the terrorists sent their members to Albania to be trained and armed in a very planned way.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, in the end of 1998 did you have intelligence that terrorists are preparing broad offensive actions in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had quite a bit of that intelligence. They called it preparations for their spring offensive.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you have any information - let us look at para 6 in this document - that even in foreign states new members were being recruited into the KLA and being sent to Kosovo, although the OSCE mission was already based there? We need para 6 of this document. And if you did have this intelligence, how did you obtain it?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I see para 6 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: We have it in English, but we need to move one page forward in B/C/S. Next page, please. This is -- this just looks like "6". It's 5, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Para 6: Throughout 1998 and especially the second half of 1998, we had intelligence. We knew that in addition to young men that were sent by terrorist staffs in Kosovo and Metohija to Albania to be trained, we knew that those training camps were also receiving young -- young men of Albanian ethnicity who were temporarily employed in other countries, who arrived from Germany via Turkey, and other countries. I would like to emphasise here that Albanians temporarily employed in Germany receive recruitment call-ups from the Kosovo Liberation Army by post, and their call-up notices bear the inscription: "Your homeland is calling on you." These call-ups also contain language that if they don't come, the Kosovo Liberation Army would come to get them. Let me just say that through this foundation, "Homeland is calling upon you," throughout 1998 and in the relevant period in 1999 taxes were collected from all ethnicity Albanians temporarily employed in European Union countries to the tune of 3 per cent of their salaries. All these moneys flowed into the fund of the Homeland is Calling foundation, were channeled to Dardanija Bank, and used to finance the purchase of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, did you have your own sources in the ranks of KLA? Did you receive information from them?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The military security service had a confidential and very broad network even in the highest echelons of the terrorist organisation in Kosovo and Metohija and in the terrorist staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: No. No, strike that. After the arrival of the OSCE mission, were units of the Pristina Corps able to conduct their normal training?

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: After the OSCE mission settled in Kosovo and Metohija, Pristina Corps units were able to conduct normal training but they had undertaken to notify all activities, including training, to the OSCE mission via the liaison team.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: General, before we leave this topic - and it's an important topic, because we have heard evidence here and exhibits, such as - let us look at 3D1033. I believe it's one of your reports in the form of telegram to the security administration of the General Staff and the security section of the 3rd Army. Look at para 3, on the last page, please, and give us a few comments. Maybe it doesn't mean much to you, but we have heard a lot of related evidence in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MOMIR STOJANOVIC
